title: Invocation Mosaic Aggregator — personal spec notes
content:
Context / motivation:
This is a personal scratchpad exploring an "invocation mosaic" primitive: a runtime component that assembles partial / heterogeneous outputs (stream fragments, tool responses, reranks, auxiliary model calls) into a single coherent response surface for the client. Goal is low-latency composition with clear failure semantics, cheap instrumentation, and small API surface for clients + SDKs.

High-level idea:
- Treat each incoming subresponse as a tile in a mosaic. Each tile has metadata (origin, sequence range, confidence, deterministic-id) and an optional patch (delta) to the aggregate response.
- Aggregator maintains an append-only timeline per request and applies deterministic merge rules to produce an ordered output stream.
- Support two modes: incremental streaming assembly (emit early stitched view) and final repair pass (post-assembly cleanup + normalization).

Architectural sketch (ASCII):

client -> ingress-router -> invocation-mosaic-aggregator -> response-stream
                            ^
                            |
               tool/model calls / kv-cache / reranker

Components:
- Tile schema (minimal): {tile_id, parent_req_id, origin, seq_start, seq_end, payload_type, payload, confidence, deps, is_final}
- Merge policy engine: ordered by seq_start, then origin-priority, then confidence. Configurable policy plug-in points: stable-sort, safelist merge, fallback filler.
- Checkpointing: small compact manifest stored with request (compact list of tiles + applied offsets). Useful for resume after disconnection.

API shapes (notes / draft):
1) Ingest endpoint (internal): POST /v1/aggregator/ingest
   payload: { "req_id": "uuid", "tile": { ...tile schema... }, "flags": ["streamable", "terminal"] }
   response: 200 / {status: "accepted", applied_offset: 512}

2) Client-facing streaming endpoint: GET /v1/requests/{req_id}/stream
   - SSE / http2 / websocket friendly; emits events: TILE_APPLIED, TILE_PATCH, CHECKPOINT, FINALIZED, WARNING
   - event envelope: {event_type, seq, view_html?, view_text?, mosaic_manifest_ref}

3) Finalize / reconcile: POST /v1/requests/{req_id}/finalize -> triggers repair pass and returns canonical payload.

Config knobs (for product+ops):
- origin_priority list (hosted-model, local-cache, reranker, external-tool)
- backfill_strategy: [no-fill | filler-template | question-reask]
- emit_early_threshold_ms: number (if mosaic cannot cover initial prefix within X ms, emit best-effort prefix)
- max_tiles_per_request: 128 default

Failure modes and policies:
- missing tile: either leave gap (emit with placeholder) or block finalization depending on request policy.
- conflicting tiles (overlapping seq ranges): deterministic tie-break by origin_priority then confidence; log conflict telemetry and attach provenance header for replay.
- malicious payloads: validate payload_type and sanitize; apply output-safety-hook before emitting.

Telemetry / observability:
- Per-request: tiles_ingested, tiles_applied, conflicts_resolved, time_to_first_view_ms, time_to_final_ms, bytes_emitted
- Span annotations: origin, merge_policy_version, manifest_ref
- Sampling: full traces for 1/1000 requests + conflict-heavy traces for debugging

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tile schema size: do we inline small reranker diffs or store external blob? tradeoffs are serialization cost vs storage complexity.
- Ordering guarantees over geo: aggregator may need causal-lamport-ish ordering when tiles come from different regions. Is eventual ordering OK for PLG clients?
- Backpressure: how does aggregator report ingress saturation to router? signal via 429 with Retry-After and optional tombstone manifest id?
- SDK ergonomics: what should client receive for partial views (HTML snippets vs text patches). Need to align with existing streaming conventions in Redwood SDKs.

Experiment plan (short):
1) Build a sidecar prototype behind a feature flag for a single internal route (rerank-heavy workloads).
2) Instrument with conflict telemetry and sample manifests to S3 for offline replay.
3) Run A/B: baseline vs aggregator with emit_early_threshold=80ms to measure latency & perceived completeness (small UX user study).

Notes to self: keep API primitives tiny; prefer composition via manifest refs rather than huge inlined tiles. Document deterministic merge rules clearly so offline replay + repro is straightforward.

References / inspiration:
- similar concept: "mosaic" in client-side UI composition (but here server-side, deterministic)
- related Redwood docs: compact-blob-format for session offload (we can reuse manifest pointers), streaming-callback-resume for resume semantics

Quick todo list (short):
- [ ] write minimal tile proto + examples
- [ ] prototype ingest endpoint and in-memory merge engine (Golang)
- [ ] small SDK shim for streaming assembly in JS/py
- [ ] create Confluence stub + invite SRE for backpressure model

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally rough — lots of open edges. Will iterate after a quick spike.
